evidence.quote: The city of Chapel Hill, is in the southeastern part of Orange County, as is Carrboro. Hillsborough is in the central part of the county

evidence.claim: Francis Nash built this Hillsborough house in 1772, before his service as a Continental Army general ended with his death at Germantown in 1777.
evidence.quote: The house was built in 1772 by Francis Nash, a politician and general of the Continental Army, who died in the 1777 Battle of Germantown

evidence.claim: William Hooper, a signer of the Declaration of Independence, bought it in 1782 and lived here until his death in 1790.
evidence.quote: it was purchased in 1782 by William Hooper, one of North Carolina's signatories of the United States Declaration of Independence, who made it his home until his death in 1790.

evidence.claim: Occoneechee Mountain rises more than 350 feet above the Eno River, reaching Orange County’s highest point.
evidence.quote: Rising more than 350 feet (110 m) from the Eno River, the Occoneechee Mountain summit is the highest point in Orange County.

evidence.claim: The natural area occupies land settled by the Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation.
evidence.quote: The land the state natural area now sits on was originally settled by the Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation

evidence.claim: A mill village occupied part of the land until 1987.

evidence.claim: State park officials began purchasing land here in December 1997.
evidence.quote: The NC Division of Parks and Recreation first purchased land at Occoneechee Mountain in December 1997.

evidence.claim: Cane Creek Reservoir supplies the Carrboro-Chapel Hill area, but its creation cost residents homes and farmland.
evidence.quote: Cane Creek Reservoir is a reservoir in Orange County, North Carolina serving the Carrboro-Chapel Hill area.

evidence.claim: As population growth outstripped University Lake’s capacity, officials considered a new water source.
evidence.quote: Proposals to build a reservoir on Cane Creek were made as the area's population was growing too large to be sustained by University Lake.

evidence.claim: The Cane Creek Conservation Association opposed the project; the Orange Water and Sewer Authority supported it.
evidence.quote: The Cane Creek Conservation Association lobbied to block the reservoir's construction, while OWASA lobbied to build it.

evidence.claim: Courts compelled landowners to sell watershed property through eminent domain, and the reservoir filled in 1989.
evidence.quote: Eventually, the courts forced local landowners to sell their land in the watershed under eminent domain, and the reservoir was built. The dam was completed in 1977, and the reservoir was filled in 1989.

evidence.claim: its creation cost residents homes and farmland.

evidence.claim: The house retains original pine floors and some fireplace mantels.

evidence.quote: the nearest brown elfin population to Occoneechee is more than 100 miles (160 km) west.
